title: 2MASS J0415-0935

catalog.source: SIMBAD via Sesame: 2MASS position (epoch about 1998-2000; used only as a search seed), proper motion Faherty et al. 2009 (AJ 137, 1), parallax Faherty et al. 2012 (ApJ 752, 56)

catalog_comparison.source: SIMBAD via Sesame: 2MASS position (epoch about 1998-2000; used only as a search seed), proper motion Faherty et al. 2009 (AJ 137, 1), parallax Faherty et al. 2012 (ApJ 752, 56)

spectrum.method: Forced ePSF photometry on native pixels at the motion-corrected (followed) position in every exposure; wavelength from the spectral WCS at that pixel; inverse-variance means in the 102 SPHEREx/SPIFF bins.

wing_attempt.summary: Experimental wing photometry was attempted on 1 saturated exposures; none had enough unflagged pixels inside the ePSF footprint (±3.3 px).

fixed_vs_follow.note: Measured at one fixed sky position, the source keeps 55% of the flux recovered by following its motion (median over 67 bins).

templates.library: SPIFF SPHEREx templates (Gagné et al. 2026; M4–Y0 field, low-gravity and subdwarf grids)
templates.reason: Best template T8 (field) with reduced chi-square 1.08 over 84 bins.

naive.description: Every exposure in time order, regardless of wavelength. Because SPHEREx sees a different wavelength in each exposure, most of this apparent change is the source spectrum, not time variability.
naive.max_ratio_basis: brightest / faintest exposure among those with S/N >= 10

matched.description: Flux in the same SPHEREx wavelength bin compared between visits. Only this comparison can reveal true time variability.

hypotheses.name: Stationary astronomical source
evidence: A stationary model is rejected: delta chi-square 1654 (about 99 sigma if the per-point errors are realistic).

hypotheses.name: Moving astronomical source
evidence: Proper motion 2239 ± 56 mas/yr from 240 exposures over 404 days; model reduced chi-square 0.70.
Parallax 195 ± 27 mas measured from SPHEREx alone.

hypotheses.name: Blended or overlapping sources
evidence: No Gaia DR3 neighbour within 2 SPHEREx pixels.

hypotheses.name: Instrumental or processing artifact
evidence: Detected in 240 independent exposures across 3 visits, on multiple detectors and wavelengths.

hypotheses.name: Known solar-system object
evidence: Positions over 404 days follow proper motion plus annual parallax of a few arcsec per year (reduced chi-square 0.70); solar-system bodies move arcseconds to arcminutes per hour and would not repeat a stellar track across visits.

verdicts.label: Known source recovered (SIMBAD via Sesame: 2MASS position)
Spectrum consistent with an ultracool dwarf (T8)

summary.headline: Moves 2.24″/yr across 240 SPHEREx exposures; spectrum matches a T8 template.
summary.one_liner: Detected in 240 independent exposures with a coherent position change. The motion-corrected spectrum is consistent with a T8 template (reduced chi-square 1.1), which supports but does not prove an ultracool-dwarf classification.

limitations: SPHEREx pixels are 6.15 arcsec; sources closer than about 1 pixel are measured as one blend.
Positions are registered to Gaia DR3 field stars with a pure shift per exposure; residual distortion is absorbed into an empirical error floor.
Fluxes use the median pixel solid angle (OMEGA_MEDIAN) and the release ePSF; absolute calibration uncertainties of a few percent are not propagated.
A template match constrains spectral type only; it does not establish mass, age or formation history.
Not one of the five NASA challenge targets; added after the Epsilon Indi B experiment to test the protocol on a second source.
follow_up: Extend the baseline with archival WISE/NEOWISE epochs to tighten proper motion and parallax.
